parsed_response.citation_summary: Polish observational study comparing organic and conventional production systems for four medicinal plant species (rosemary, peppermint, lemon balm, sage). Finds organic plants have higher dry matter, vitamin C, phenolic acids, and flavonoids, while conventional plants have higher carotenoids. No quantitative effect sizes reported. Study conducted over two years but specific years not stated.

parsed_response.methodology: Comparative observational study comparing bioactive compound content (dry matter, vitamin C, carotenoids, polyphenols) in four medicinal plant species grown under organic vs conventional production systems over two consecutive years. Analytical methods included Polish Standards for dry matter and vitamin C, and high-performance liquid chromatography for carotenoids and polyphenols.
